events.feedback:
Readability & Engagement

Accessibility: Excellent balance between popular culture history and botanical evolutionary biology. Terms like sympatric speciation and monoecious are paired directly with clear explanations.

Flow: Connecting Queen Victoria's parlour palm obsession to the modern houseplant trade creates a strong hook for general park visitors scanning the QR code.

Accuracy Check

Botanical Facts: Spot-on. Howea forsteriana is endemic to Lord Howe Island, flowers out of sync with Howea belmoreana (sympatric speciation linked to calcareous soils), takes up to 6 years for fruit/seeds to mature, and was described by Ferdinand von Mueller before Odoardo Beccari established the genus Howea.

events.summary: Thirteen targeted corrections applied: bloom season changed from spring to November–December per UF/IFAS; inflorescence description corrected to 'below the leaves on 3.5-foot stalks, male and female on same inflorescence'; the unsupported six-year fruit-maturation figure replaced with 'several years' (UF/IFAS gives 3–4 years); speciation language softened from settled fact to possibility; 'every' Kentia softened to 'many'; 'all of her residences' and 'the defining plant' softened; 'at least 15 years' softened to 'around 15 years'; 'the flesh is not edible' updated; native_notes sharpened to distinguish cold-hardiness from Florida-climate suitability; and a new other_notes paragraph added flagging UF/IFAS's 'short-lived in Florida' rating.

Overall Assessment
The Kentia Palm page is shaping up exceptionally well. It captures the rich historical and biological narrative of Howea forsteriana while framing it effectively for a local Florida audience.

Summary of Strengths & Key Integration Highlights

Captivating Cultural Hook: Leading Quick Hits with the Victorian parlour craze and the RMS Titanic's Palm Court immediately hooks general visitors before introducing complex botanical concepts.

UF/IFAS Context Realism: Clearly communicating that cold-hardiness (Zone 9b) does not automatically equal ease of growth in Florida's extreme summer heat/humidity gives high value to local gardeners.

Sympatric Speciation Narrative: Explaining how the Kentia and Belmore Sentry palms diverged on a tiny island due to offset flowering times turns a standard plant sign into a memorable evolutionary biology lesson.
